channel.title: Rother Daily
channel.description: Local news for Bexhill, Battle, Rye and the Rother villages, morning and evening.

item.title: CIL funds £1.3m for Bexhill hub and village projects
item.description: Rother District Council has allocated £1.3 million from the Community Infrastructure Levy to local projects. The CIL is a charge on developments over a certain size to fund the building and upgrading of public facilities that will be needed to support growth.

item.title: East Sussex council to re-house Old Hastings House residents
item.description: East Sussex County Council is working to find new accommodation for residents of Old Hastings House care home in Hastings after failing to agree on increased placement costs.

item.title: Wear a mask: reduce the spread of respiratory illnesses
item.description: East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust is asking people to wear face masks in some areas of its hospitals and services.

item.title: Rother council seeks views on extending dog control rules
item.description: Rother District Council has launched a six-week consultation on its Public Space Protection Order (PSPO) for dogs. The current order is due to expire in January 2027, and the council proposes to extend it for a further three years until 2030.

item.title: Winter thrushes arrive around Rye
item.description: Hundreds of Fieldfares and Redwings are arriving around Rye from Scandinavia and Siberia to escape harsh northern weather. David Bentley, writing for Rye News, notes that these winter thrushes are currently settling into the area as autumn colours peak.

item.title: Bexhill shops stay open late for Christmas event
item.description: Shops in St Leonards Road and the lower end of Sea Road in Bexhill stayed open until 7pm last Friday, 20 November, for a late-night shopping event. The initiative aimed to bring Christmas cheer to residents and visitors.

item.title: Bexhill public toilets to become cafe with accessible WC retained
item.description: Rother District Council has approved plans to convert the public toilets building at Little Common Roundabout in Bexhill into a cafe. The decision was made by planning officers who reviewed the application from Jessica Jones of Crema Del Cafe Ltd.

item.title: Rye veteran to walk 40 miles for charities
item.description: John Hobbs, an Army veteran in his 81st year, is set to walk 40 miles from Rye to raise funds for two local charities. He will start at 6am on Saturday 28 November, walking towards Lydd and back, then to Camber and back twice. The route includes checkpoints at Jury's Gap and the entrance to the Lydd military training area.

item.title: Bexhill community hub opening date revealed
item.description: A date has been announced for when a new community hub in Bexhill town centre is expected to open. Work has started on the building, located at 34 Devonshire Road, where scaffolding has appeared outside the premises. More than £519,000 has been allocated to support the creation of the hub at the former Edinburgh Woollen Mill building.

item.title: Rye resident shares one-year heat pump experience
item.description: Andrew Pickles, a Rye resident, has published his first-year experience of living with a heat pump system. He notes that while installation costs are high and the process can be disruptive, the system has been almost entirely positive for his 1960s house.

item.title: Rye Literary Institute hosts first festive market
item.description: The newly restored Rye Literary Institute is set to hold its first ever Festive Market on Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December.

item.title: Rye council backs Pugwash statue and multi-faith prayer space
item.description: Rye Town Council has agreed to support the placement of a bronze Captain Pugwash statue in Gun Gardens, subject to planning approval. The proposal was put forward by the Pugwash Statue Committee, represented by Alan Dickinson, on 25 November. While the idea received unanimous support, councillors debated the exact location to ensure the memorial has maximum effect.

item.title: Rye church clock faces costly restoration after 40 years of wear
item.description: The famous clock at St Mary the Virgin in Rye is in need of urgent restoration, according to a report by Andrew Bamji and Roy Abel in Rye News. While the internal mechanism was restored in 2012 by the Cumbria Clock Company, the exterior fittings have suffered significant damage from weather, ageing, and pigeons over the past four decades.

item.title: Rye Film Club returns to Community Centre on 4 December
item.description: Rye Film Club is set to return to the Rye Community Centre on Friday 4 December.

item.title: Bexhill councillors debate High Street Rental Auction plans
item.description: Bexhill Town Council has discussed Rother District Council’s proposal to use High Street Rental Auction powers in the town centre. The scheme aims to bring persistently vacant commercial properties back into use.

item.title: Rye Bowls Club wins third place in 2026 Mermaid League
item.description: Rye Bowls Club has been awarded third place for the 2026 Mermaid League season. The award was presented at the recent annual league dinner, which was hosted by Judith Blincow at the Mermaid Inn in Rye.

item.title: Rye station hosts riversong exhibition and anthology
item.description: A creative writing exhibition called Riversong is currently on display in Rye train station. The show features poems, riddles, and invocations inspired by walks along the Tillingham, Brede, and Rother rivers.

item.title: Rye Players mount biggest-ever panto with local help
item.description: Rye Players are preparing to stage their largest town pantomime yet, Cinderella, in December. The production is being built on the goodwill of local residents and professionals who have donated their time and skills.

item.title: Camber Sands named among UK's best beaches for winter walks
item.description: Camber Sands has been named one of the best beaches in the UK for a winter walk. The site, which features the only sand dune system in East Sussex, was included on Beachlets' list of the top 10 beaches for the season.

item.title: Catsfield crash: Two children leave hospital
item.description: Two children, aged six and three, have been released from hospital after being struck by a car in Catsfield, Sussex Police said.

item.title: Pett Level residents demand action on flooding and water quality
item.description: Residents of Pett Level gathered at The Smugglers Retreat on Monday 23 November to press the Environment Agency and Southern Water for better management of flood risks and water pollution. The public meeting, led by MP Helena Dollimore, brought together representatives from Southern Water, the Environment Agency, East Sussex Fire & Rescue Service, and Pett Parish Council.

item.title: Ten projects win £900,000 bio-bead compensation for Rye and Camber
item.description: Ten local projects have been selected to share £900,000 in reparation funding from Southern Water. The money follows the accidental release of plastic bio-beads from the company’s Eastbourne wastewater treatment works in October 2025.

item.title: Bexhill presbytery conversion plans refused by council
item.description: Plans to convert the former presbytery next to St Mary Magdalene Church in Bexhill into new homes have been refused by Rother District Council planners.

item.title: Rother council forecasts £668,000 revenue surplus
item.description: Rother District Council’s Overview and Scrutiny Committee met on 16 November to review the council’s financial position and performance for the second quarter of 2026/27. A report to the committee, prepared by the Director of Resources, forecasts a revenue surplus of £668,000 at the end of the year. This surplus is driven by favourable financing costs.

item.title: On this day, 1947: Charles Tippet collapses at Rye Golf Club
item.description: On 26 November 1947, Charles Tippet collapsed and was found on the floor of his office at Rye Golf Club in East Sussex. He had just finished showing his friend, the Bishop of Ely, around the place. By 1945, Tippet had been given the job of reviving the club, but it proved too much for him. Edith was called to his side, but two days later Major Tippet died at the age of 56.

item.title: Bexhill and Battle MP speaks on Civil Service Pension Scheme in Parliament
item.description: Dr Kieran Mullan, the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle, spoke in the House of Commons on Tuesday 24 November regarding the Civil Service Pension Scheme.

item.title: Bexhill Christmas Light Switch-On set for 5 December
item.description: Bexhill-on-Sea’s Christmas Light Switch-On and Christmas Market is scheduled for Saturday, 5 December. The event will take place on Western Road and Devonshire Square, running from 3pm until 7pm.

item.title: New cancer support hub to open at Eastbourne DGH
item.description: A new dedicated cancer support hub is arriving at Eastbourne District General Hospital. The facility will provide information, practical guidance, and emotional support for patients and families across East Sussex.

item.title: Ombudsman upholds complaint against East Sussex Council over SEN plan
item.description: The Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman has upheld a complaint against East Sussex County Council regarding the handling of a child’s Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan. The decision, issued on 13 October 2026, found fault in how the council managed the case between February 2025 and March 2026.

item.title: A26 Eridge bridge inspected; Burwash wall repaired
item.description: East Sussex Highways has completed principal inspections of the A26 bridge over the railway at Eridge. The work required special closures of the railway line, arranged through Network Rail, to allow inspectors to access the structure safely.

item.title: Man arrested after car hits three people in Catsfield
item.description: A 72-year-old man has been arrested following a serious collision between a car and three pedestrians in Catsfield. The incident occurred on The Stream at approximately 8.30am on Wednesday, 25 November.

item.title: Battle campsite named UK's most unique in 2026 awards
item.description: Beech Estate Campsite in Battle has been named the most unique site in the UK at the 2026 Campsites.co.uk Camping and Glamping Awards.

item.title: On this day, 1833: The cricketing priest who played for Cambridge in 1855
item.description: John Sumner Gibson was born on 25 November 1833 in Chester. He was an English priest and a first-class cricketer, though his sporting career was brief. His single recorded first-class match was the 1855 University Match against Oxford, playing for Cambridge University. In that game, he batted low in the order, scoring 8 and 23, and did not bowl.

item.title: Jazz guitarist Nigel Price to play Bexhill's Blue Note
item.description: Award-winning jazz guitarist Nigel Price is set to make his first appearance at the Blue Note Jazz Club in Bexhill on Sunday 6 December.

item.title: Council extends loan for Blackfriars housing scheme to 2029
item.description: Rother District Council has agreed to extend the Development Facility Agreement for its housing company until 31 July 2029. The decision was made by the Shareholder Executive Committee on 18 November at the Town Hall in Bexhill-on-Sea.

item.title: County leader criticises government reorganisation plan
item.description: East Sussex County Council has responded to the Government's call for further evidence on local government reorganisation. Cllr Andy Woolley, the council leader, stated that the Government has not explained the reasons for its proposal to create a new unitary authority for East Sussex, excluding East Saltdean, Peacehaven and Telscombe.

item.title: De La Warr Pavilion staircase windows removed for heritage repair
item.description: The distinctive staircase windows at Bexhill’s De La Warr Pavilion have been removed as major internal refurbishment work begins. Scaffolding and security fencing are now in place around the area, with the curved glass and metal frames taken down for specialist restoration.

item.title: Severe Weather Emergency Protocol active in Rother until Friday
item.description: Rother District Council has activated its Severe Weather Emergency Protocol (SWEP) in response to current and forecasted weather conditions. The protocol is a locally agreed procedure designed to minimise the risk of harm to people sleeping rough by providing emergency accommodation.

item.title: Battle Abbey Nursery visits Southlands care home for 104th birthday
item.description: Children from Battle Abbey Nursery in Bexhill recently visited Southlands care home to celebrate a resident’s 104th birthday. The preschool group, known as the Oaks, created a card featuring 104 balloons made from their fingerprints and performed a rendition of Happy Birthday.

item.title: Little Common come from behind to beat Pagham 4-1
item.description: Little Common secured a 4-1 victory over Pagham at the Recreation Ground on Saturday, securing three much-needed points in the SCFL Premier.

item.title: Russell Brand effigy burned at Robertsbridge bonfire night
item.description: An effigy of comedian Russell Brand was set alight during the bonfire celebrations in Robertsbridge on Saturday, November 21. The event saw the village’s Station Road and High Street described as a "river of fire" as the procession moved through the streets.

item.title: Hundreds attend St Richard's fourth annual Christmas Fayre in Bexhill
item.description: St Richard's Catholic College in Bexhill hosted its annual Christmas Fayre on Saturday, 21 November, with hundreds of people attending the event.

item.title: Battle care home hosts Tommy Tea Party for veterans
item.description: Hazel Lodge Care Home in Battle hosted a Tommy Tea Party to raise funds for the Royal British Veterans Enterprise charity.

item.title: Person injured following two-vehicle collision on A259 between Eastbourne and Bexhill
item.description: A two-vehicle collision involving a motorcycle and a car occurred just before 7.40am on Monday, 23 November, on the A259 between Eastbourne and Bexhill.

item.title: Rother council reports 14 concluded conduct complaints
item.description: Rother District Council’s Standards Committee is due to meet on Tuesday 1 December to review a six-monthly update on councillor conduct.

item.title: Tributes paid to Bexhill panto legend Ken Stevens
item.description: Tributes have been paid to Kenneth Stevens, a well-known figure in Bexhill who died peacefully in his sleep on November 6, aged 90, at the Conquest Hospital. His niece, Kate, said he was a beloved local presence, often remembered for writing, performing in, and making costumes for pantomimes.

item.title: Bexhill zebra crossing relocated to improve safety
item.description: A zebra crossing in Bexhill town centre has been relocated further south, the county council said. The move allows motorists to complete a full turn from Endwell Road before stopping at the crossing, improving safety for pedestrians.

item.title: Battle Christmas events begin with fair and light switch-on
item.description: Battle Town Council has published a schedule of festive events for the town, starting on Saturday 28 November. The day features a Taste of Sussex at Battle Abbey School, a Christmas Fair at St Mary’s Church, and Santa’s High Street Parade.

item.title: Bexhill hospital unit gets first portable ultrasound system in trust
item.description: The Bexhill Irvine Unit has received a new SonoSite MT Ultrasound System, the first of its kind introduced within East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust. The portable device is designed to support specialist rehabilitation and injection services for patients with complex needs following a stroke, brain injury, or neurological diagnosis.

item.title: Political accountability: Battle boarding house licence approved despite objections
item.description: A licensing panel has approved a Premises Licence for Battle Abbey School Boarding House on Whatlington Road. The licence covers alcohol sales, late night refreshment, and regulated entertainment, primarily for weddings and functions during school holidays. Hours are set from 12:00 to 00:30, Monday to Sunday. A report to the committee notes that eight representations objected to the application, citing concerns about crime, public nuisance, safety, and child protection. The officer recommendation was to determine the application, and the panel approved it.

item.title: Political accountability: East Sussex County Council, week from Sunday 15 November to Saturday 21 November 2026
item.description: East Sussex County Council confirmed decisions on transport and adult social care this week. The Lead Member for Transport and Environment noted decisions made on 20 July 2026 regarding the Pan-Sussex Minerals and Waste Plan Proposal and the Highway Vegetation Management Policy review. The Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Health confirmed decisions on residential and nursing provider payments, the Integrated Health and Wellbeing Service contract, and Disability Related Expenditure.

item.title: Political accountability: MP raises Beckley school PE funding concerns in Commons
item.description: Dr Kieran Mullan, the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle, raised a local issue in the Commons on Monday 16 November. He spoke during Topical Questions about the impact of government reforms on physical education funding at Beckley Church of England primary school. He stated that teachers and parents reported a "massive drop" in provision and asked the Minister to agree to meet him to discuss the situation in Beckley and other schools.

item.title: Political accountability: Dollimore backs Visitor Levy and Immigration Bill in Commons
item.description: Helena Dollimore, the Labour (Co-op) MP for Hastings and Rye, voted in favour of the Visitor Levy (England) Bill Second Reading on Monday 16 November. The bill passed with 296 votes to 96.

item.title: Bexhill beat Midhurst 5-1 to climb to sixth
item.description: Bexhill put five past Midhurst and Easebourne in the latest in a long run of Polegrove fixtures which has seen the Pirates move steadily up the table. The win continues a strong run of form for the Pirates, who have been climbing steadily since September.

item.title: Crowhurst Park Lodges wins Hoseasons guest satisfaction award
item.description: Crowhurst Park Lodges in Battle has been named the Relax & Explore Small Park destination in the South of England at Hoseasons’ 21st annual Diamond Awards.

item.title: On this day, 1885: Maid of Kent rescue
item.description: On 24 November 1885, the Rye lifeboat was called to the aid of the fishing smack Maid of Kent. This incident is recorded in the service history of the station, which operated from Camber Sands for 44 years before closing in 1901. The rescue was part of a long tradition of maritime assistance in the area, following earlier calls to vessels such as the steamship Medea in 1882 and the brigantine Cyrus in 1871.
